findings.issue: The RecoveredNotSignedIn sentence is assigned to _error but never rendered when a replacement sheet came back: the error card `@if (_error is { Length: > 0 })` lives only inside the `@if (_newSheet is null)` branch, so with «أصدر ورقة استرداد جديدة» ticked the person sees the new sheet and «احفظ الورقة الجديدة الآن» and is never told that the workspace did not open and that الوكيل must be closed and opened again. The builder's note claims the sentence stays on screen; it does not in that path.
findings.fix: In the `else if (_newSheet is { } sheet)` branch, render the sentence as well — e.g. add `@if (_error is { Length: > 0 }) { <WCard Variant="WSemanticVariant.Warning" Icon="info" Desc="@_error" /> }` under the sheet card (or set `DialogDesc` to `_error` while `_recoveredWithoutSession` is true).

findings.issue: RecoveredNotSignedIn without a replacement sheet leaves the form on screen with _code/_password/_confirm cleared and CodeVerified still true; the confirming button still reads «تعيين كلمة المرور والدخول» and pressing it re-enters SubmitAsync, which fails the strength check and overwrites the important sentence with «8 أحرف على الأقل». The person is nudged to redo a recovery that has already happened.
findings.fix: Gate the button on the flag: make `ConfirmLabel`/`ConfirmIcon` return the closing label and `ConfirmAsync()` return `CloseAsync()` whenever `_recoveredWithoutSession` is true, not only when `_newSheet is not null`.

findings.issue: RollBack deletes the key file and the database with their siblings but not the vault blobs already written by StoreAttachmentsAsync (VaultStore.Write for the logo, guide, report template, letter template). A failure after the first attachment leaves encrypted files in the vault folder whose vault key was wiped with the abandoned key file: dead bytes that no later installation can read or account for.
findings.fix: Collect the hashes returned by VaultStore.Write in a local list inside ActivateAsync and, in RollBack(committed==false), delete each corresponding vault file with the same swallowed IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException guard the other deletes use.

findings.issue: _lastCountedCode survives a successful recovery and a successful sign-in, so the last wrong code counted stays 'already counted' forever: after the counter has been reset, re-typing that exact code costs no attempt. Harmless against a real brute force (which uses fresh codes) but it makes the counter's state depend on history it should have forgotten.
findings.fix: Clear `_lastCountedCode = null;` on the success path of RecoverAsync (next to the Success result), and ideally also when LoginService.OpenSessionAsync resets the profile counters.

findings.issue: The lock-out is re-evaluated only in OnPasswordChanged and at the top of SignInAsync, so a person who simply waits out the announced pause without touching the keyboard keeps seeing a disabled «دخول» and the danger card until they type a character. The round-3 fix covers the typing case only.
findings.fix: Start a short TimeProvider timer while `_lockedOut` is true (e.g. every 15 s, the same cadence LockService uses) that clears `_result` and calls StateHasChanged once `Login.LockedUntil()` is null, and dispose it in the component's Dispose.

THE SEVEN ROUND-2 FINDINGS, RE-CHECKED IN THE CODE.
Medium 1 (activation rollback) — genuinely fixed. `committed` is set only after _session.Adopt, the DiskFull result and the general rethrow both run RollBack first, and RollBack removes installation.key with its .tmp/.bak and wakeel.db with -wal/-shm/-journal, swallowing only IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException. Because AlreadyActivated proved neither existed on entry, the machine is restored. The walkthrough test blocks the database path, asserts the throw, the absent key file, IsActivated/AlreadyActivated false, and then that the same file, sheet and code activate on the second try and both secrets still work — not a tautology. One residue remains: vault blobs already written are not swept (low finding 3).
Medium 2 (recovery ordering) — genuinely fixed. DbSession.Open runs before a single wrap is rebuilt; `saved` splits the paths; the pre-save failure returns DatabaseUnreadable with the key file byte-identical (the test asserts byte equality plus the old password and old code still working) and the post-save failure returns RecoveredNotSignedIn carrying the new sheet rather than a lie. The one gap is presentational, not cryptographic: the sentence explaining what happened is not drawn in the sheet branch (low finding 1).
Low 3 (W05 cached lock) — fixed for the typing path; the idle path is still cached (low finding 5).
Low 4 (LockService key leak) — fixed; the catch zeroes machineDbKey/machineVaultKey. I also checked the success path: AccountSession.Unlock zeroes dbKey itself and takes only the vault key over, and the finally's ReferenceEquals guard on vaultKey is correct in both the machine-wrap-present and machine-wrap-absent cases.
Low 5 (dropped keystrokes) — fixed with a pending-text loop; the bUnit test fires two texts without awaiting the first and waits for «تحقّق من الرمز», which fails without the loop.
Low 6 (deletable counter) — mitigated as described: SignInProfile.Missing raises LockRounds to at least 1 on an activated machine. The residual limit is honestly stated in open_issues and is an owner decision, not a defect.
Low 7 (unlimited recovery codes) — fixed. Verify and RecoverAsync both refuse while LockOutInForce stands and count a wrong-but-well-formed code through LoginService.RecordWrongPassword, de-duplicated against the last counted text. The walkthrough test drives five distinct wrong codes to a standing lock, proves the right code and RecoverAsync are refused, proves a repeated text costs nothing, and proves recovery works once the wait is over. The only nit is that the de-duplication key is never cleared after success (low finding 4).

SECURITY RE-CHECK OF THE PARTS THE ROUND TOUCHED. Password → PasswordWrap, RecoveryWrap, MachineWrap (DPAPI via IPlatformProtector) and AdminWrap are still created for both DbKey and VaultKey, each with its own fresh salt, as ARCHITECTURE §3 requires; device seeds are sealed with the DbKey. No key is written in the clear, every failure path zeroes its buffers, the staging folder is cleared on success, and the sign-in card is machine-sealed. Verify/RecoverAsync return states rather than throwing out of keystroke handlers, and neither the code nor the password survives in dialog state after use. The three open_issues the builder reports are accurate and are specification questions for the owner, not defects.

CONCLUSION. Build and tests are green, every round-2 finding was actually addressed with tests that fail when the fix is removed, all of W02–W07 are present and render, and nothing above rises past low. Accepted; the five low findings are worth folding into a later polish pass, finding 1 first.
